prompt: Put what a real browser does with the shop's page in order, from the bytes to the screen.
items: Fetch the bytes of the page
Parse the HTML into a DOM
Match the CSS rules to each element
Lay out every box: its size and place
Composite the layers onto the screen
trap: Layout needs the matched styles first: a box cannot be sized before its rules are known.

prompt: This course's Playwright tests run in Chromium with no window. What kind of browser is that?

choices.text: A simulated browser, because nothing is shown on a screen
choices.why: No window is not the same as no layout. Headless Chromium still lays the page out and paints it into memory.

choices.text: The whole browser, laying out and painting into memory
choices.why: Right. That is why lesson 16 could take screenshots of it and lesson 7 could measure 400 pixels.

choices.text: A DOM library like jsdom, started by Playwright for speed
choices.why: Playwright never swaps the browser for a library; it drives a real Chromium build.

choices.text: A browser that runs scripts but skips the CSS
choices.why: Headless Chromium applies every rule; the Menu button was hidden by CSS in it, at 1280 pixels.

prompt: Which step of a browser's work does a simulated browser leave out entirely?

choices.text: Parsing the HTML
choices.why: It parses: jsdom found the eight cards with ordinary selectors.

choices.text: Running the page's scripts
choices.why: jsdom ran `app.js` and drew the cards once it had a `fetch`.

choices.text: Layout
choices.why: Right. With no layout there is no size or position, which is why `scrollWidth` came back 0.

choices.text: Matching CSS rules
choices.why: Partly kept: jsdom matched `min-width` on the basket and reported 384px.

prompt: Zombie's `visit` called back with 0 cards, and two seconds later there were 8. What does that show?

choices.text: The shop drew the list twice, empty the first time
choices.why: There was one drawing; it happened after the callback, when `/api/products` answered.

choices.text: Its idea of loaded left out the request for the cards
choices.why: Right. Its log said the event loop was empty before `GET /api/products` went out.

choices.text: Zombie cannot run `app.js`, so something else drew them
choices.why: It ran it: eight cards appeared two seconds later, drawn by that script.

choices.text: The server was slow to answer the first request of the page
choices.why: The requests were fast; they simply started after Zombie had already called back.

prompt: What did `npm view` show about the state of Zombie.js?

choices.text: A release last month, built on the same jsdom 30 as this lesson
choices.why: The newest release is 6.1.4, and it pins jsdom 11.12.0.

choices.text: That it was removed from npm and no longer installs
choices.why: It is still there and still installs, with a screen of deprecation warnings.

choices.text: Last release 2018, pinning jsdom 11.12.0
choices.why: Right. Nineteen major versions of jsdom behind, with a deprecated `request` underneath.

choices.text: That the team behind Playwright maintains it now
choices.why: Its maintainers are its own authors, and nothing has been published since 2018.

prompt: HtmlUnit found 8 cards on `/ssr` and 0 on `/`. Why none on `/`?

choices.text: Its Rhino engine could not parse the `async` function on line 3 of `app.js`
choices.why: Right. No script ran, so nothing drew the cards. On `/ssr` they came in the HTML.

choices.text: The home page is broken in every browser
choices.why: Chromium and jsdom both drew eight cards from the same page.

choices.text: Three seconds was too short a wait for `/api/products`
choices.why: The request was never sent: the script that sends it failed to compile.

choices.text: HtmlUnit does not run JavaScript at all
choices.why: It does run it, through its own engine; this script used syntax the engine does not know.

prompt: Match each tool with where the page's JavaScript runs in it.

pairs.right: A fork of Mozilla Rhino, inside Java
Node's own V8, in a separate context
V8 inside a browser that also lays out and paints

prompt: A Java team's suite runs on `HtmlUnitDriver` and is green. A user reports that a button does nothing in Safari. What did the green suite establish about Safari?

choices.text: That the button works there, since both follow the standard
choices.why: Following a standard is what every engine claims; lesson 10 runs three real ones because they still differ.

choices.text: Nothing: it ran in an engine no user has
choices.why: Right. A pass in HtmlUnit is a pass in Rhino and HtmlUnit's DOM, not in Safari's JavaScriptCore and WebKit.

choices.text: That the defect is in Safari, not in the page
choices.why: The suite never ran in Safari, so it holds no evidence about where the fault lies.

choices.text: That the button worked in Chrome too
choices.why: No Chrome ran either; `HtmlUnitDriver` starts no browser at all.

prompt: For jsdom to run the shop's scripts, the option is written `runScripts: '___'`, a name that warns the sandbox is not foolproof.
A script opens the shop with `runScripts: 'dangerously'` and leaves out `resources: 'usable'`. What happens?

choices.text: jsdom refuses to start unless both options are given together
choices.why: Each option is independent; jsdom starts happily with either.

choices.text: The cards are drawn but unstyled
choices.why: Nothing draws them: the script that would is never downloaded.

choices.text: `app.js` is never fetched, so the list stays empty
choices.why: Right. Without it jsdom loads no subresource, scripts in `<script src>` included.

choices.text: The inline scripts fail while the external ones run as usual
choices.why: It is the other way round: inline scripts run, and external ones are not fetched.

prompt: The first `simulated/home.mjs` ended with `ReferenceError: fetch is not defined`, although Node 22 has `fetch`. Why?

choices.text: Node's `fetch` still needs an experimental flag on version 22
choices.why: Node 22 has `fetch` with no flag; `shop.mjs` itself calls it.

choices.text: The shop's server refuses requests that do not come from a browser
choices.why: No request was sent; the error came before any.

choices.text: The page's window is jsdom's, and it has no `fetch`
choices.why: Right. The page's globals are jsdom's, not Node's, and jsdom 30.1.2 implements no `fetch`.

choices.text: The Node in use is older than the versions jsdom 30.1.2 supports
choices.why: npm did warn about 22.22.0, but the fixed script ran on that same Node without an error.

prompt: In Chromium, at 360 pixels wide, the shop's `scrollWidth` was 400. What number did jsdom report for the same page?
Somebody moves lesson 7's check `scrollWidth <= 360` into a jsdom test to make the suite faster. It passes. What has the move done?

choices.text: Fixed the defect, since the basket no longer overflows
choices.why: `style.css` did not change; Chromium still measures 400.

choices.text: Made the check faster and just as good
choices.why: It is not as good: it now compares 0 with 360 on every page, broken or not.

choices.text: Turned it into a check that passes on every page
choices.why: Right. Without layout every width is 0, so the test can no longer fail, which is worse than having no test.

choices.text: Made it fail, because jsdom has no window
choices.why: It passed: jsdom answers with 0, not with an error.

prompt: Above 600 pixels the Menu button is `display: none`. jsdom's `click()` on it set `aria-expanded` to true. Why could it?

choices.text: jsdom did not know that the stylesheet hid the button
choices.why: It knew: `getComputedStyle` reported `display` as `none` one line earlier.

choices.text: Its `click()` goes straight to the element, with no pointer
choices.why: Right. Nothing asks whether the element is visible, covered or zero-sized; Playwright's click asks all three.

choices.text: The media query in `style.css` hides it on phones and nowhere else
choices.why: Above 600 pixels it is hidden for everyone; Chromium refused to click it at 1280.

choices.text: jsdom waited until the button became visible, then clicked it
choices.why: jsdom has no auto-waiting, and the button never became visible.

prompt: Which of these did jsdom 30.1.2 report as `undefined` on the shop's window?

choices.text: `matchMedia`
choices.why: Right: a page cannot ask a media query's question there.

choices.text: `IntersectionObserver`
choices.why: Right: nothing scrolls into view where nothing has a position.

choices.text: `querySelector`
choices.why: It is there; every script in the lesson used it.

choices.text: `getComputedStyle`
choices.why: It is there, and it reported `min-width` as 384px.

prompt: Why is `simulated/ssr.test.mjs` a good fit for jsdom?

choices.text: It needs no script and no layout, only the HTML the server sent
choices.why: Right. Every question it asks is answered the same in jsdom and in Chromium.

choices.text: jsdom runs `/ssr`'s late script faster than Chromium
choices.why: The test runs no scripts at all; neither option is set.

choices.text: It checks that the buttons on `/ssr` can be pressed
choices.why: It checks that each button carries the right `data-id`; whether a person can press it is a browser's question.

choices.text: Playwright cannot read server-rendered HTML
choices.why: Lesson 6 read it with Playwright's `request` fixture.

prompt: Which of these checks could move from a Playwright test to a jsdom test without losing anything?

choices.text: Nothing on the home page is wider than a phone's 390-pixel window
choices.why: Width needs layout; jsdom would answer 0 and pass.

choices.text: The Menu button opens and closes the navigation on a narrow phone
choices.why: It depends on a media query and on a click a person can make, neither of which jsdom models.

choices.text: The HTML of `/ssr` has a card for every product the API lists
choices.why: Right. It reads the tree the server sent, which is identical in both.

choices.text: Search shows its results only after the last of its requests answers
choices.why: Lesson 3's race depends on real requests in a real page; through a shim it would test the shim.

prompt: A cookie banner covers the Pay button on a checkout page. A jsdom test clicks Pay and passes. A customer cannot pay. What did the test miss?

choices.text: That the banner's script failed
choices.why: The banner works perfectly; the trouble is where it is drawn.

choices.text: That the Pay button is under something, which only layout knows
choices.why: Right. jsdom's click goes straight to the element; a pointer lands on whatever is on top.

choices.text: That the button has the wrong label
choices.why: The label is in the DOM, and jsdom reads it like any browser.

choices.text: That the test needed a longer wait for the banner to go away by itself
choices.why: No wait helps: the banner never moves, and jsdom never asks where things are.

prompt: `shop.mjs` lends the page Node's `fetch`. A tester uses it to check that the shop refuses a request from another site. What is wrong with that test?

choices.text: Node's `fetch` applies none of the browser's rules between sites, so it tests the shim
choices.why: Right. The check is about what a browser enforces, and no browser code is in the path.

choices.text: jsdom cannot send a POST request
choices.why: The banana's `POST /api/basket` went through the same shim.

choices.text: The shim forgets the page's address
choices.why: It resolves each address against `window.location.href`, which is how `/api/products` worked.

choices.text: Nothing: the shim is the browser's own `fetch`
choices.why: There is no browser here; the shim hands the request to Node.

prompt: jsdom's README names two features outside its scope: layout, and ___, which is why clicking the Search link left the address at `/`.
